title: Configuration file parser
prompt:
Parse the configuration file given at the end and print its settings. Its lines are numbered from 1. Process them in order, using these rules:
- A line that is empty after removing its leading and trailing spaces, or whose first non-space character is `;` or `#`, is ignored.
- A line that, with leading and trailing spaces removed, starts with `[` and ends with `]` starts the section NAME, where NAME is the text between the brackets with surrounding spaces removed. A section can be started again later; settings then go into it again.
- Any other line that contains `=` is a setting; any other line without `=` is the error `line N: syntax error`. For a setting, split the line at its first `=`. If the character directly before that `=` is `+`, the setting appends (`KEY += VALUE`) and that `+` is not part of the key; otherwise it assigns (`KEY = VALUE`). KEY is the text before the `=` (without that `+`) and VALUE the text after it, both with surrounding spaces removed. If KEY is empty, the line is the error `line N: empty key`; otherwise, if no section has been started yet, it is the error `line N: no section`.
- If VALUE is at least 2 characters long and starts and ends with `"`, the value is the text between those quotes, kept exactly as it is (nothing in it is replaced). Otherwise every reference in VALUE is replaced, from left to right: `${S.K}` by the current value of key K in section S, and `${K}` by the current value of key K in the section the line belongs to. If a referenced key has no value yet (no earlier line set it), the line is the error `line N: unknown reference R`, where R is the text between `${` and `}` of the first such reference, and the setting is not made.
- An assignment gives the key its value, replacing any earlier value. An append makes the value the old value, a comma and the new value; if the key has no value yet, it simply gets the new value.
Print each error line as it happens, then a line `---`, then every setting as `SECTION.KEY = [VALUE]` (the value between square brackets), sorted by section name and then by key name, both in plain character order.
The file, one line per item, each line given between the backticks:
1. `; settings`
2. `title = demo`
3. `[server]`
4. `host = example.org`
5. `port = 8080`
6. `name = "  main  "`
7. `port = 9090`
8. `[paths]`
9. `root = /srv`
10. `logs = ${paths.root}/logs`
11. `data = ${root}/data`
12. `bad line here`
13. `[ server ]`
14. `url = http://${host}:${port}/`
15. `alias = ${missing}`
16. `= value`
17. `   # indented comment`
18. (an empty line)
19. `[paths]`
20. `tags += web`
21. `tags += api`
22. `root = /var`
23. `quoted = "${root}"`
24. `[extra]`
25. `formula = x=y+1`
26. `mirror = ${server.url}${paths.root}`
27. `broken = ${paths.data}${server.nope}`
28. `half = "open`
expected_output:
line 2: no section
line 12: syntax error
line 15: unknown reference missing
line 16: empty key
line 27: unknown reference server.nope
---
extra.formula = [x=y+1]
extra.half = ["open]
extra.mirror = [http://example.org:9090//var]
paths.data = [/srv/data]
paths.logs = [/srv/logs]
paths.quoted = [${root}]
paths.root = [/var]
paths.tags = [web,api]
server.host = [example.org]
server.name = [  main  ]
server.port = [9090]
server.url = [http://example.org:9090/]
